subject: mathematics
title: Adding numbers up to 10
summary: Put two groups together and count how many there are altogether.

lesson.text: Adding means putting things together to find how many there are altogether. We use the sign + (plus) for adding and = (equals) for the answer.
You don't have to count from 1 every time. Start from the bigger number and count on.

steps: Start at 6 and keep it in your head.

lesson.text: 4 + 1 and 1 + 4 give the same answer, 5. So start with the bigger number: it is quicker.
Use your fingers, bottle tops or seeds. Seeing the things helps you understand the sum.

questions.explanation: Start at 4 and count on 3: 5, 6, 7. So 3 + 4 = 7. (1 is what you get if you take away, not add.)

questions.prompt: Emeka has 5 sweets. His sister gives him 2 more. How many sweets does he have now?
questions.explanation: Start at 5 and count on 2: 6, 7. Emeka has 7 sweets.

questions.prompt: Which number goes in the gap: 6 + ? = 10
questions.explanation: Count on from 6 to 10: 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 4 steps, so 6 + 4 = 10.
4 + 5 = 9, not 10. The others are all pairs that make 10.
